description:
FILED s414 (Opus) while probing the differences between the copies of #387
family 2 (ExprToCL::gen_funcall_form's element arms).  Not the family's own
bug â an independent one the probe uncovered.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL, both run):
  my $s = "aXbXc"; $s =~ /X/g;        print pos($s);      # perl 2, PCL 2   OK
  my @a = ("aXbXc"); $a[0] =~ /X/g;   print pos($a[0]);   # perl 2, PCL undef
  my %h = (k=>"aXbXc"); $h{k} =~ /X/g; print pos($h{k});  # perl 2, PCL undef
Also true through a ref (@$r[0], $r->[0], ${$r}[0]) â every element spelling.

DIAGNOSIS (emission read, runtime read â not a guess):
  `$a[0] =~ /X/g` emits   (p-=~ (p-aref @a 0) (p-regex "/X/g"))   <- the VALUE
  `pos($a[0])`   emits    (p-pos (p-aref-box @a 0))               <- the BOX
The scalar case emits the box on BOTH sides, which is why it works.  In
cl/pcl-runtime.lisp the matcher stores the position in *p-match-pos* keyed by
what it was handed (`string`, ~:15876/15919) and `p-pos` (:3263) reads it
keyed by `var` when `(p-box-p var)` â so the two use DIFFERENT keys for an
element.  Consequences: (a) pos() on an element always reads undef; (b) the
position that IS recorded hangs off the CL string OBJECT, so `while ($a[0]
=~ /X/g)` does advance and terminate (probed: two iterations, correct) but
the state is shared by any other place holding that same string object and
is lost when the element is reassigned.

FIX SHAPE (not attempted): make the `=~` binding of an element lvalue pass
the BOX, the way pos/tied already do â i.e. the same "container + key, take
the box" rule as `_elem_container_key` (#387 family 2).  Probe first whether
p-=~ wants a box everywhere (s/// on an element already works and must not
move: `$a[0] =~ s/X/Y/` is correct today).  Guard rows: the three shapes
above + the while-loop iteration + `pos($a[0]) = N`.
subject: SILENT WRONG: pos() on an array/hash ELEMENT is always undef â the `=~` binding passes the element VALUE while pos()/tied() pass the BOX, so /g position is recorded under the string object and read under the box
